name: AnybandUI
author: WurliMonkhaven, neostryder
description: Wurli Monkhaven's AnybandUI, rebuilt for Neo Angband. You can play with the mouse: click the map to move and act, keep your character, status and messages in panels, and compare gear in an item window before you wear it. Each feature has its own switch and starts off, and none of them change the game's rules.

settings.title: CRT strength
settings.description: How dark the scanlines are, from none at 0% to full at 100%.

settings.title: Low health tint strength
settings.description: How deep the red tint gets when your hit points run low.

settings.title: Death burst strength
settings.description: How bright the burst is when your character dies.

settings.title: Floor item glow strength
settings.description: How bright the glow is around artifacts, cursed items and unlearned runes on the floor.

settings.title: Sleep mark strength
settings.description: How clearly the marks show over sleeping creatures.

settings.title: Presence haze strength
settings.description: How thick the violet haze is around unique creatures.

settings.title: Combat ring strength
settings.description: How bright the combat rings and the blast flashes are.

rules.title: Item panel
rules.description: Opens a panel with your pack, equipment and quiver on separate tabs, a search box, and each item in its game colour. Anything on the floor where you stand is listed above the tabs. Click an item to select it.

rules.title: Item inspection
rules.description: Shows the game's full description of the item you select in the item panel, the same text the Inspect command gives.

rules.title: Equipment comparison
rules.description: When you select something you could wear, a table compares your current equipment with the change: speed, armour, to-hit, damage, blows, stats and resistances. Only properties your character knows are counted, and a checkbox also shows the stats that stay the same.

rules.title: Quantity picker
rules.description: When the game asks how many, the item panel offers One, Half and All buttons and a box for any other number.

rules.title: Item choice list
rules.description: When the game asks you to pick an item, the item panel lists the choices so you can click one instead of typing its letter.

rules.title: Mark new items
rules.description: Items you have just picked up are marked NEW in the item panel, and a stack that grew shows how many were added, until you click it.

rules.title: Item action buttons
rules.description: Adds buttons under the selected item for wielding, taking it off, dropping, inscribing, using and ignoring it. Only the actions the game would accept right now appear.

rules.title: Item rules
rules.description: Lists your ignore settings and auto-inscriptions in the item panel, and lets you change them there. Search to add a rule for any kind of item or ego you have seen.

rules.title: Click to walk
rules.description: Left-click a tile in the dungeon view to step there, or to travel there if it is further away. Clicking a creature next to you attacks it, and while you aim, a click picks the target. Shift-click a tile next to you to run that way, and Ctrl-click any tile to make it your target.

rules.title: Tile action menu
rules.description: Right-click a tile in the dungeon view for a menu of what you can do there: walk, look, target, pick up, open or close a door, tunnel, disarm a trap, or take the stairs. The game decides which of these the tile allows. While you aim, the menu offers Select tile and Cancel.

rules.title: Gold aiming path
rules.description: While you choose a target, a gold line shows the path your spell or missile would take to the tile under the pointer. The game works the path out itself, so the line stops wherever the shot would.

rules.title: Walking route preview
rules.description: Draws a gold line along the route you would walk to reach the tile under the pointer, worked out the same way the travel command plans it.

rules.title: Character card
rules.description: Replaces the character column with a card: your name, race and class, bars for hit points, spell points, food and experience, your stats, gold, armour and speed, and a health bar for the creature you are tracking. Hover a bar or stat to see its numbers. On a version of the game with movable panels, the card is a panel of its own in the column's place.

rules.title: Status badges and dungeon card
rules.description: Replaces the status line with a badge for each timed effect, coloured by whether it helps or harms you, and a card showing depth, light, the level feeling and the terrain underfoot. Hover a badge to see how many turns it has left. While the Borg or another mod is playing for you, a badge says which one.

rules.title: Message log
rules.description: Replaces the message line with a scrolling log. Repeated messages fold into one line with a count, and a search box finds an older message. When the game stops at -more-, click the log to carry on.

rules.title: Accessibility: high-contrast display
rules.description: Boosts contrast and colour separation over each finished frame, in text mode and with tiles, across the dungeon, maps, menus and this mod's panels.

rules.title: Accessibility: colourblind correction
rules.description: Applies a red-green colour correction over each finished frame, in text mode and with tiles, across the dungeon, maps, menus and this mod's panels.

rules.title: First-encounter alerts
rules.description: The first time this character meets a kind of monster, or picks up an artifact, a small card appears in the corner with its name and native depth. A monster's card carries a threat badge: Unique, Deadly (well out of depth), Out of depth, or First sighting. The card never takes the keyboard or blocks a click, and clears itself after a few seconds. Each character keeps its own record.

rules.title: Itemize the quiver in the Inventory subwindow
rules.description: The Inventory subwindow lists each stack of ammunition or thrown weapons in your quiver by name, under a --Quiver-- heading, instead of a count such as "in Quiver: 7 missiles".

rules.title: Sharpen shrunken tiles
rules.description: Draws graphics tiles with crisp pixel edges when they are shrunk, instead of the smoothed default. Pixel-art tilesets often look sharper this way at small zoom levels.

rules.title: Zoom, pan and responsive layout
rules.description: Ctrl-= and Ctrl-- make glyphs or tiles bigger or smaller, and the view fits as many whole rows and columns as the window holds. Ctrl-Arrows pan, Ctrl-Wheel zooms the area under the pointer, and a two-finger pinch or swipe zooms or pans on touch. The zoom level is kept for every character.

rules.title: Accessibility: enlarged display
rules.description: Starts the display at a larger, easier-to-read cell size. It works even with zoom and pan turned off, and does not change your saved zoom.

rules.title: Drag to pan
rules.description: Hold the middle mouse button and drag to move the dungeon view.

rules.title: Follow the character
rules.description: Keeps the view on your character as you move. Panning away pauses it, and Ctrl+Home brings the view back and starts following again.

rules.title: Keep the target in view
rules.description: While you aim, the view moves so the targeting cursor stays on screen.

rules.title: Centre on a new level
rules.description: Arriving on a new level centres the view on your character.

rules.title: Hover cards on the map overview
rules.description: Resting the pointer on a cell of the map overview, or holding a finger on it, opens a card with a magnified tile and what you know about that cell: terrain, creature, item, trap or shop. It shows nothing your character has not seen.

rules.title: Hover cards on the dungeon view
rules.description: Resting the pointer on a tile of the dungeon view opens a card with what you know about it: the creature or character there with a small health bar and a line of what you remember about its kind, the terrain, and up to five items on the floor. The delay before a card opens is one setting shared with the map overview's cards, 550 ms to start with.

rules.title: Full-level map overview
rules.description: The (M)ap screen shows every square of the level you know, shrunk to fit, with markers for you, the stairs and the shops, and an outline of what the main view shows. The mouse wheel zooms at the pointer, dragging pans, and Fit floor and Centre on player buttons sit beside the map.

rules.title: Schematic map
rules.description: Draws the map overview as flat blocks of colour for walls, doors and floor instead of glyphs or tiles, which is easier to read when the whole level is shrunk.

rules.title: Spell panel
rules.description: Lists the spells in each book you carry, with mana, fail rate and whether you can cast or learn each one, plus its description. Click Cast or Study, or double-click a spell to cast it.

rules.title: Quickbar
rules.description: Thirty slots on the number keys, with a second row on Shift and a third on Ctrl, for spells, potions, scrolls, wands, activations and simple commands such as picking up or taking the stairs. Each slot shows its mana cost, charges or count and greys out when you cannot use it. Right-click a spell or drag it onto a slot to assign it. The number keys go back to the game inside menus and prompts, and each character keeps its own slots.

rules.title: Blast preview
rules.description: While you aim a ball or breath, shades every tile the blast would reach, worked out by the game itself, in the colour of its element. A breath is shown as a ball of the same radius.

rules.title: Rest panel
rules.description: Adds a Rest button, and answers the game's own rest prompt, with a choice of how long to rest: until you are fully recovered, until either hit points or mana are full, or for a set number of turns. While you rest, it shows how long is left and a button to stop. Danger still interrupts rest as usual.

rules.title: Store window
rules.description: While you are in a store or your home, shows its stock and your pack side by side. Click an item to select it.

rules.title: Store prices
rules.description: Shows the price of each item in the store window.

rules.title: Store comparison
rules.description: When you select something you could wear, compares it with what you have in each slot it could go in, the same way the item panel does.

rules.title: Store buttons
rules.description: Adds Buy, Sell, Stash, Retrieve and Leave buttons to the store window. The store then asks how many you want and shows the price before you confirm. Older versions of the game allow only Leave.

rules.title: Store questions
rules.description: When the store asks how many or whether to accept a price, answers it with buttons in the store window instead of the keyboard.

rules.title: CRT display
rules.description: Gives the dungeon view the look of an old monitor: slightly richer colours, faint scanlines, and a slow band of light that sweeps down the screen. The sweep stops when your system asks for reduced motion.

rules.title: Low health warning
rules.description: Tints the dungeon view red once your hit points drop below the game's own hit point warning, deepening as they fall, with a pulse unless your system asks for reduced motion. With that warning turned off, it starts below 30 percent.

rules.title: Death burst
rules.description: Draws a burst on your character's square at the moment of death.

rules.title: Floor item glow
rules.description: Makes a soft glow around items you know about on the floor: gold for an artifact, red for a known curse, and blue for a rune you have not learned yet.

rules.title: Sleeping creature marks
rules.description: Puts a small mark above each sleeping creature you can see.

rules.title: Unique presence haze
rules.description: Surrounds each unique creature you can see with a violet haze, heaviest around the one guarding the final quest, which is Morgoth unless a mod changes the quests.

rules.title: Combat rings and flashes
rules.description: Draws a brief ring where a spell is cast, where a blow or shot lands or misses, where a creature dies, where someone heals, and at both ends of a teleport. The squares a ball or breath hits flash in the colour of its element. Only things your character sees are drawn.
